name: What uninstall deletes and what survives
plain: Uninstall wipes app storage on both systems, but some data survives in backups, the cloud or the keychain.
meaning: Residual data is how a company recognises a returning user. Survivors: iOS Keychain, iCloud data, Android backups, shared media and server records.

android.persistence: Deletes internal and app specific external storage; shared media, Auto Backup copies (25 MB) and server data remain
android.note: Backed up data restores at next install if Auto Backup was on; MediaStore files you created remain

ios.persistence: Deletes the app container; Keychain items, iCloud Drive and CloudKit data, and server records remain
ios.note: Keychain items survive uninstall and reinstall on the same device (docs and developer reports); restored backups also restore keychain

limits.headline: Can't keep most data after uninstall, though backups, cloud and keychain may restore some
limits.user_action: You uninstall the app from Settings or delete it from the Home Screen
can: Restore backed up data on the next install if Auto Backup was on
Keep files it made in shared media on Android
Bring back Keychain items on iPhone after a reinstall on the same device
cannot: Keep its private storage, which is wiped on both systems
Keep Android Keystore entries; they go with the app
Keep anything you also removed from your cloud backup
limits.reach_label: Local data goes, some data survives
limits.differs: Both wipe app storage. iPhone Keychain items usually survive, and Android restores from Auto Backup.

story.what_it_is: Deleting an app clears its storage, but some data stays in backups, the cloud or the keychain.

marketing.name: Offering account deletion in your app
marketing.pitch: Apple requires apps that let you create an account to also let you delete it in the app.

story.for_you: You delete the app thinking it is gone for good. Later you reinstall and find your login, scores or settings still there, because some data lived somewhere else.
story.for_makers: Makers use what survives to recognize a returning customer. It helps restore progress, and it also lets a person be re identified after a reset.

use_cases.example: You delete a game and come back to find your progress waiting.
A streaming app remembers your profile after a reinstall.
A marketer matches a returning install to the same person using a kept ID.
A store keeps your cart on the server and finds it again.
A bank app spots a device that deleted the app and came back with a different login.
A fitness app returns with your history from the cloud.
A team groups before and after a reinstall as one user.

story.android_note: Backed up data returns if Auto Backup was on. Files in shared media stay.
story.ios_note: Keychain items stay after delete and return on reinstall, including from a restored backup.

technical_bounds: Keychain survival is documented behavior with caveats
Server side data is outside the device

history.change: Keychain introduced, persists across uninstall by design
Apps with account creation must offer account deletion in app
